posts.title: Expo spotlight: Gulfood 2027
posts.caption:
Gulfood runs 15 to 19 March 2027 in Dubai, across Dubai World Trade Centre and Expo City Dubai.
For food and halal exporters looking at GCC buyers, it is the date to plan around.
UAE business visas are usually arranged before travel. Full 2027 calendar on our site.

posts.title: Expo spotlight: HANNOVER MESSE 2027
posts.caption:
Hannover Messe 2027: 5 to 8 April, Hannover Exhibition Grounds.
Automation, robotics and energy tech for Philippine factories and economic zones.
Germany is in the Schengen area, so book visa appointments early. Calendar link in bio.

posts.title: Expo spotlight: 141st China Import and Export Fair (Spring Canton Fair)
posts.caption:
The Spring Canton Fair is expected in three phases from mid-April to early May 2027. Dates are the usual pattern, not yet published.
Pick the phase that matches your product category.
The China business (M) visa needs four to six weeks. Start early.

posts.title: Expo spotlight: FOODEX JAPAN 2027
posts.caption:
FOODEX Japan 2027: 9 to 12 March at Tokyo Big Sight.
A route to Japanese importers for Philippine food exporters, and a place for food buyers to source Japanese products.
Japan needs a short-term business visa through accredited agencies.

posts.title: Expo spotlight: Salone del Mobile.Milano 2027 (with Euroluce)
posts.caption:
Salone del Mobile.Milano runs 13 to 18 April 2027 at Fiera Milano Rho, with Euroluce for lighting.
Useful for furniture exporters, designers and hotel fit-out teams.
Italy is Schengen: apply to the country of your main stay.

posts.title: Expo spotlight: IFEX Philippines 2027
posts.caption:
Closer to home: IFEX Philippines 2027, 20 to 22 May at the World Trade Center Metro Manila.
Local producers meet foreign buyers, and retailers find new suppliers.
Hosting overseas buyers or visitors? We can handle their hotels and transfers.

posts.title: 2027 trade-show calendar: January & February
posts.caption:
January and February 2027 on one page: CES, NRF, Heimtextil, Ambiente, MAGIC and more.
A filled dot means the organiser has published dates; an open dot means expected.
Save this for planning. Full calendar on our site.

posts.title: 2027 trade-show calendar: March
posts.caption:
March is the busiest month on our 2027 calendar, with 21 trade expos.
Here are ten with confirmed dates, from Frankfurt to Tokyo and Dubai.
Save it and check the rest on the site.

posts.title: 2027 trade-show calendar: April
posts.caption:
April 2027: Hannover Messe, Salone del Mobile, the Hong Kong spring fairs and the first phase of the Canton Fair.
Nine highlights here; the full list is on our calendar.
Visas for April trips should start in February.

posts.title: 2027 trade-show calendar: May
posts.caption:
May 2027: food shows in Singapore, Bangkok, Chicago and Amsterdam, and IFEX here in Metro Manila.
Save this list for the food and hospitality team.
Full calendar on our site.

posts.title: 2027 trade-show calendar: June to August
posts.caption:
Mid-year 2027 is quieter: Computex, Seoul Food, GILE, the Summer Fancy Food Show and Hong Kong's Food Expo.
A good window to plan the busy autumn season.
Full calendar on our site.

posts.title: 2027 trade-show calendar: September
posts.caption:
September 2027: IFA Berlin, IAA Mobility, Big 5 Saudi and a run of Shanghai and Shenzhen fairs.
Several China dates are expected rather than confirmed; we check them before booking.
Save this list.

posts.title: 2027 trade expos at a glance
posts.caption:
Our 2027 calendar lists 102 trade expos in 21 countries, with dates marked confirmed or expected.
March and April are the busiest months; mid-year is quieter.
Filter it by sector and month on our site.

posts.title: Carousel: autumn 2027 trade-show calendar
posts.caption:
Autumn 2027 in five slides: October and November trade expos, and what to do while dates are still expected.
Save it for your planning meeting.
Full calendar on our site.

posts.title: Destination guide: Germany
posts.caption:
Germany has 12 trade expos on our 2027 calendar, in Frankfurt, Cologne, Düsseldorf, Hannover, Berlin and Munich.
Philippine passport holders need a Schengen visa for business visits.
Book the appointment early in peak season.

posts.title: Destination guide: UAE
posts.caption:
Dubai on the 2027 calendar: Intersec, WHX, Gulfood, Big 5 Global and Automechanika.
The UAE business visa is usually arranged before travel, often through the host or hotel.
We confirm each case when we prepare your proposal.

posts.title: Destination guide: Japan
posts.caption:
Japan on our 2027 calendar: FOODEX, GREEN×EXPO, CEATEC and the Japan Mobility Show.
Philippine passport holders apply for a short-term business visa through accredited agencies.
Allow time for the paperwork.

posts.title: Destination guide: USA
posts.caption:
The USA on our 2027 calendar: CES, NRF, MAGIC, High Point, the NRA Show and the Summer Fancy Food Show.
A B-1 business visa needs an embassy interview, and waiting times can be long.
Plan well ahead.

posts.title: Destination guide: Hong Kong
posts.caption:
Hong Kong hosts the HKTDC fairs through the year: toys, jewellery, electronics, lighting, gifts and food.
Philippine passport holders can visit visa-free for 14 days.
Crossing to Shenzhen or Guangzhou still needs a mainland China visa.

posts.title: Destination guide: Vietnam
posts.caption:
Vietnam on our 2027 calendar: VIFA EXPO in Ho Chi Minh City and Vietnam Expo in Hanoi.
Short business visits are visa-free for Philippine passport holders, as across ASEAN.
Length of stay differs by country, so we confirm before you fly.

posts.title: Visa required or visa-free: 10 destinations
posts.caption:
Ten common business destinations for Philippine ordinary passport holders, at a glance.
Rules change, so we confirm each case when we prepare your proposal.
Full table on our visa page.

posts.title: Hong Kong 14 days, Macao 30 days visa-free
posts.caption:
Hong Kong: visa-free for 14 days. Macao: 30 days.
The catch: a day trip to Shenzhen or Guangzhou still needs a mainland China visa.
Planning a fair-and-factory trip? We sort both.

posts.title: Schengen visa for European trade fairs
posts.caption:
Frankfurt, Milan, Paris, Cologne: most European fairs sit inside the Schengen area.
Apply to the country of the fair or your main stay, and book the appointment early in peak season.
We prepare and file; the embassy decides.

posts.title: US B-1 business visa: start early
posts.caption:
Heading to a US trade show? Philippine passport holders need a B-1 business visa, with an embassy interview.
Waiting times can be long, so start well ahead of the show.
We check documents and track the application.

posts.title: UK Standard Visitor visa for business
posts.caption:
The UK Standard Visitor visa covers business meetings and trade fairs.
We check the documents first, prepare the forms with each traveller and track the application.
Details on our visa page.

posts.title: Visa paperwork, off your desk
posts.caption:
Four steps we take on every business visa: document check, forms and filing, the appointment, and tracking until the passport is back.
The embassy decides; we make sure the file is complete.
More on our visa page.

posts.title: Carousel: China business (M) visa documents
posts.caption:
Going to the Canton Fair or visiting factories in China? The business (M) visa needs five things, set out in this carousel.
Allow four to six weeks.
Save it and share it with your travel admin.

posts.title: Flights and hotels, booked to your policy
posts.caption:
Sending people abroad for audits, training or sales calls?
We compare fares across airlines, spell out the baggage and change rules, and book hotels near where your team works.
Changes are handled for you.

posts.title: Trade show trips that end in orders
posts.caption:
A trade show trip is more than a flight and a badge.
We handle buyer registration and invitation letters, hotels near the venue, hall planning by product category, and supplier meetings around fair days.
See the 2027 calendar on our site.

posts.title: On the ground: interpreters, transfers, factory routing
posts.caption:
The trip is decided on the ground.
Bilingual interpreters by the half or full day, airport transfers and drivers, factory visit routing, and introductions to forwarders for samples and cargo.
All arranged with the rest of the trip.

posts.title: Finance-ready from the first quote
posts.caption:
For finance and admin teams: every proposal is itemised, so you can approve line by line.
Repeat travellers, groups and annual programmes are quoted on corporate terms.
Invoices and official receipts are issued in your company's name.

posts.title: Nothing is booked or paid until you approve
posts.caption:
One rule we work by: nothing is booked or paid until you approve.
You get an itemised proposal first and approve it line by line.
Request a corporate proposal on our site.

posts.title: One coordinator per trip
posts.caption:
Every trip gets one coordinator.
Visas, flights, hotels, registration and ground transport are handled together, so nothing falls between suppliers.
Based in Metro Manila.

posts.title: Trade fair packing checklist
posts.caption:
A simple packing list for trade fair trips.
The one most people forget: printed copies of the visa and registration.
Save it for your next fair.

posts.title: Six questions for every supplier meeting
posts.caption:
Six questions worth asking at every supplier booth or factory visit.
Write the answers down the same day, so you can compare quotes like for like.
Save this for your next sourcing trip.

posts.title: Plan the halls before fair day
posts.caption:
Large fairs are too big to walk at random.
Map the halls by product category, list must-see booths and group them by hall.
We include hall planning in every trade show trip.

posts.title: After the fair: follow-up checklist
posts.caption:
The orders come from what you do after the fair.
Sort contacts, follow up in the same week, request samples and compare quotes like for like.
Need a factory visit next? We route it.

posts.title: Five lines every trip budget should show
posts.caption:
A trip quote with one total is hard to approve.
Ask for airfare, hotel, visa, registration and ground services as separate lines.
That is how every ExpoBusiness proposal is laid out.

posts.title: Carousel: trade show trip timeline
posts.caption:
A working timeline for a trade show trip: 12 weeks to register, 8 to start visas, 6 for hotels and flights, 2 for meetings and ground.
It is a guide, not a rule; visa lead times differ by country.
Save it for your team.

posts.title: Delegations that move as one programme
posts.caption:
Trade missions, conferences and incentive trips need the whole group moving as one.
Group airfare, rooming lists and coaches, group visa filing and a pre-departure briefing, and the events in between.
For chambers, associations, LGUs and companies.

posts.title: Group airfare and seat blocks
posts.caption:
Moving a delegation starts with the flight.
We arrange group airfare and seat blocks, manage the name list as people confirm, and source charter flights on request.
Tell us the headcount and dates.

posts.title: Rooming lists, coaches and a delegation lead
posts.caption:
Arrival day sets the tone for a delegation.
Rooming lists checked with the hotel, coaches between hotel, venue and visits, and a delegation lead on the ground.
Interpreters by the half or full day.

posts.title: Group visa filing and pre-departure briefing
posts.caption:
The hardest part of a delegation is often the paperwork.
We check every delegate's documents, file the group's visas and track them, then hold a pre-departure briefing.
The embassy decides; we make sure the files are complete.

posts.title: Meeting venues, business dinners and galas
posts.caption:
A trade mission is also its meetings and dinners.
We arrange meeting venues, business dinners and gala events around the trade programme, with interpreters where needed.
Tell us the group size and the city.

posts.title: Planning a delegation? Send us four things
posts.caption:
Planning a trade mission or delegation for 2027?
Send us the destination, dates and headcount. We reply with an itemised proposal you can approve line by line.
Nothing is booked until you approve.
